I've thought about self-deprecating humor a lot and here are my observations or theories on it:

  • No one likes someone who can't take a joke. Self deprecating humor is a good way of signaling you can receive jokes without taking them personally.
  • If your content is garbage or if you are a shithead, being in front of it and calling yourself out before someone else can call you out on it is less painful to go through.
  • A lot of humor can be very mean spirited and if you aren't sure about the sensitivity of the people around you can turn the mean jokes on yourself and no one will have their feelings hurt.
  • Some people are very insecure and observe non-insecure people using self deprecating humor effectively. They view it as a way they can indulge in their insecurity in a socially acceptable way.
  • Some people probably use it as a way to fish for positive reinforcement. (For example they may be looking to get comments like "Oh man, don't be so hard on yourself, your youtube content is dope!")
  • When you are trying to think of things to make fun of, it's easy to find things about yourself that can be made fun of since most people are very critical of themselves. For a lot of us there is probably quite a bit of material to work with. (See, there's some self-deprecation right there. :P)
  • A lot of comedians and public figures use it effectively and we tend to repeat jokes and comedy styles that we observe because they are funny. I can think of a few routines Louis CK did making fun of himself that were genuinely funny in spite of being pure self-deprecation.

For me, I think it's interesting to observe the difference between a confident person using self deprecation and an insecure person using it. You can tell the difference if you pay attention. Hell, you probably notice the difference without making a conscious effort to do so, anyway. I know I do.

I am interested in what others have to say about this style of humor.
